thread.title: Bill Fleckenstein: Now Is The Time To Short Tesla (Podcast) - Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA)

author: Quoth the Raven
title: Bill Fleckenstein: Now Is The Time To Short Tesla (Podcast) - Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA)
text:
Bill Fleckenstein is an outspoken market commentator that, in my opinion, doesn’t get as much mainstream media as he should. The last time he appeared on my podcast, back in October 2018, he spent time pitching me on why he thought Apple ( AAPL ) was a perfect short. Now, only about two months later, Apple has seen its share price decline precipitously, validating Bill's assumptions and paying him on his short.
Apple is down 27% in the two months since Bill was on my podcast.
AAPL data by YCharts
On my most recent podcast, Bill disclosed to me that he no longer was short Apple but that he did think now was the time to short Tesla ( TSLA ). Though he wasn’t especially critical of Elon Musk, Bill thinks that market sentiment, combined with the company’s financials may mean that now is a timely place to launch a short position. He says that he once thought that shorting Tesla was "impossible" but that now, the company seems "vulnerable".
"Even if the company's fundamentals weren't as bad as they are, I think the company would wind up going lower with the tape next year anyway," Bill says. He also discusses how the capital structure and bond prices are going to make it tough for the company to pull off "threading the needle" type transactions that the company will need to consummate going forward.
Bill gave his reasoning as part of a broader market analysis in which he concluded that more downside for the markets could very well be likely. We also continued our ongoing discussion on monetary policy, interest rates and the Federal Reserve.
From there, we went on to discuss gold and other precious metals. Bill explained to me some of his favorite gold mining companies and what he looks for when valuing these types of companies – aside from just the spot price of gold or a company's price to earnings ratio. Bill went into depth about several companies and management teams that he owns and has owned for a while.
Bill is a professional money manager with over 30 years of experience.
He has written daily commentary on market action since 1996 and FleckensteinCapital.com launched in 2003.
